proposals.title: Complete the Krinner mixing-chamber budget: TWPA pump lines, drive-attenuator dissipation and flux-pulse dissipation
proposals.description: The validated mxc_wiring_heat_budget sums 58 drive lines (passive), 50 flux lines (passive + DC bias) and 8 output lines and its own assumptions say 'active drive-line dissipation and TWPA pump lines are not included'. Krinner et al. budget all of these for the same 50-qubit, 124-line processor (their Fig. 10) and report that the MXC load is about 30 % of the cooling power, split about equally between passive and active loads. Three terms are missing: (i) the 8 TWPA pump lines, which use the drive-line attenuator/thermalisation scheme, so their passive MXC load equals the measured drive-line value 0.013 uW; (ii) the qubit drive signal dissipated in the 20 dB MXC attenuator: Krinner's average required power at the processor is -78 dBm = 1.585e-11 W, so the attenuator dissipates (100-1) x 1.585e-11 W = 1.57 nW per qubit drive line (their 10 dBm test confirms the dissipation lands on the attenuator's own stage); (iii) flux pulses for two-qubit gates: R_eff,MXC x I_p^2 x D = 0.15 uW/mA^2 x (0.4 mA)^2 x 0.33 = 7.92 nW per flux line, which reproduces the published 0.20(1) uW for 25 lines. With these terms the profile's MXC load rises from 4.864 uW to 5.442 uW. Against Krinner's own measured 19 uW at 20 mK this is 28.6 % (published: 'about 30 %'), whereas the current model gives 25.6 %: the extension reproduces the published budget, the current model under-counts it by about 11 %. dBm is logarithmic and not representable in CryoLean, so the drive power is entered in W.
proposals.equation_latex: \mu\Big[n_d q_d + n_p q_p + n_o q_o + n_q\,P_{QP}\,(G_{MXC}-1) + n_f\big(q_f + p_{dc} + R_{\mathrm{eff}}\,I_p^{2}\,D_p\big)\Big] \le P_{\mathrm{cool}}(T_{\mathrm{doc}}),\qquad T_{\mathrm{doc}} \le T_{\mathrm{op}}
proposals.validity: Same region as mxc_wiring_heat_budget: cooling power documented at T_doc <= T_op (here exactly 20 mK), all parameters non-negative. Additional assumptions, each a named parameter so users can change them: attenuator configuration with 20 dB at the MXC (G_MXC = 100); at least ~99 % of an attenuator's dissipation flows to its own stage; the -78 dBm average presumes Krinner's gate schedule (alternating single/two-qubit gates, 33 % duty, equal pi and pi/2 share); flux pulses of 0.4 mA at 33 % duty; TWPA pump active load at the MXC omitted (only a CP figure is published). Only meaningful where the cooling power is a system-level value measured on the experimental flange (Bluefors), see TH3.

proposals.title: Illumination-heating limit for vitrified samples: per-grid devitrification threshold measured with a 77 K stage, valid only where the stage can be held at or below that reference
proposals.description: In cryo-fluorescence / cryo-CLEM the heat load that published procedures actually budget is the heating of the grid square by absorbed illumination, which must keep the vitreous sample below ~136 K; the cryostat's cooling power is irrelevant at these powers because the heat must cross a poorly conducting support film. The profile's own source (Last et al. 2023) measured the maximum 488 nm power density per grid type with the grid bars held at 77 K (their Table 1) and imaged at 186.5 W/cm2 on UltrAuFoil gold film (limit 254 W/cm2). Huebinger & Bastiaens 2026 (also a profile source) show heating is governed by absorption in the support and reaches steady state within <20 ms, so a steady-state check is appropriate; Berkamp et al. 2023 (profile source) list 'reduce the excitation light power' as the remedy for devitrification. Mojiri et al. 2025 add the configuration dependence: thresholds fall steeply when the base temperature rises (gold: ~250 W/cm2 at 77 K -> ~125 W/cm2 expected at 95 K) and vacuum cryostats at 77 K tolerate laser doses comparable to open LN2 stages for metallic grids. Model: compare the user's illumination with the measured threshold, valid only where the configuration can hold the stage at or below the 77 K reference. A colder heat sink can only lower the sample temperature at equal absorbed power (steady conduction with positive conductivity is monotone in the boundary temperature), so a pass established at 77 K remains a pass below it, while a warmer stage is outside the evidence. A second, optional relation encodes the authors' own rule of operating at 70 % of the threshold.
proposals.equation_latex: I_{\mathrm{ill}} \le I_{\max}(\mathrm{grid},\,488\,\mathrm{nm},\,T_{\mathrm{ref}}=77\,\mathrm{K})\quad\text{valid if } T_{\mathrm{lo}}(c) \le T_{\mathrm{op}} \le T_{\mathrm{ref}},\ \lambda = 488\,\mathrm{nm};\qquad \text{optional: } I_{\mathrm{ill}} \le 0.7\,I_{\max}
proposals.validity: Stage (grid-bar) temperature T_op <= 77 K and reachable by the configuration (cap temperature.range sel lo <= T_op); wavelength exactly 488 nm (two inequalities); grid type equal to a Table-1 row (no extrapolation across mesh sizes or films); rows reported only as '> 690 W/cm2' (Formvar, SiO) are lower bounds and may only appear in a validity gate (PASS or UNSUPPORTED, never FAIL); illumination longer than ~20 ms (steady state); transfer from the open LN2 stage to vacuum cryostats is supported for metallic films (Mojiri) and less certain for carbon films.

proposals.title: Sound cooling-power semantics for every heat-budget model: bare cold-head vs system capacity, base-temperature check, and FAIL only against an upper-bound slot
proposals.description: Both implemented heat models compare a load with the cooling power documented at the highest temperature <= T_op. The retrieved datasheets show why this rule cannot carry new heat-load models soundly. (1) Several 'cooling power' values are bare cold-head ratings: Lake Shore CCS '1 W at 4.2 K bare head cooling power'; CRX probe stations 'CCR with 1 W cooling power at 4.2 K'; Oxford OptistatDry 'Cold head cooling power 0.2 W at 4.2 K (60 Hz) 0.16 W at 4.2 K (50 Hz)'. They exclude the cryostat's own parasitic loads (windows, probe arms, wiring), and the catalog's 0.2 W for the BLV is the 60 Hz figure. (2) For CRX-VF (10 K), CRX-4K (4.5 K base, control from 5 K) and OptistatDry BLV/TLEX (6.5 K with the four standard windows) the configured stage cannot even reach the temperature at which the rating is quoted: base temperature is 'a balance of the ... cooling capacity and the parasitic loading' (Howe et al.), so at its own base such a stage has no spare capacity at all. (3) Dilution-refrigerator specifications are system values measured on the experimental flange and already include posts and shield radiation (Krinner), so loads added on top of them are not double counted. (4) Capacity is non-decreasing in temperature and steep near the base (Schmidt et al.: 240 mW at 4.2 K but 80 mW at 3 K), so the value at the highest documented temperature <= T_op is a lower bound on capacity at T_op: a FAIL against it is not sound unless T_doc = T_op. Proposed rule: PASS only through a validity gate L + P_par <= Q(T_lo) with T_base <= T_lo <= T_op (P_par = 0 for system-level ratings; for bare cold-head ratings P_par must be documented, e.g. the cold-head capacity at the configuration's base temperature); FAIL only through L <= Q(T_hi) with T_hi the lowest documented temperature >= T_op. This is expressible today as two coupled entries per model: a fail-capable relation, and a pass gate whose comparison sits in 'validity' with a trivially true relation (a violated validity bound gives UNSUPPORTED, never FAIL).
proposals.equation_latex: \mathrm{FAIL} \Leftarrow L > Q_{\mathrm{doc}}(T_{hi}),\ T_{\mathrm{op}} \le T_{hi};\qquad \mathrm{PASS} \Leftarrow L + P_{\mathrm{par}} \le Q_{\mathrm{doc}}(T_{lo}),\ T_{\mathrm{base}} \le T_{lo} \le T_{\mathrm{op}};\qquad \text{otherwise NEED\_MORE\_INFORMATION}
proposals.validity: Applies to every coupled model whose rhs is a cooling_power.at_* slot (Joule heating, MXC wiring budget, TH1, TH6, TH7 and future heat models). Requires monotone non-decreasing capacity in temperature (already an assumption of the implemented models) and a 'basis' attribute on each cooling-power record: system_net (experimental-flange guarantee) or bare_cold_head (+ mains frequency). For T_op = T_doc (MXC at 20 mK) both entries use the same slot and the rule reduces exactly to today's behaviour.

proposals.title: Window radiation and probe-arm conduction as documented base-temperature anchors (monotone bracket) instead of a Stefan-Boltzmann estimate
proposals.description: Manufacturers document the thermal effect of the two parasitic loads users change most. Optical windows: Quantum Design Oxford gives the OptistatDry base temperature as 6.5 K with the four standard Spectrosil WF windows and '<3 K' (BLV) / '<4 K' (TLEX) with blanks fitted, and states that all windows are user-changeable. Probe arms: Lake Shore gives the CRX-4K base as 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.0 K with 2 / 4 / 6 arms (control from 5 / 6 / 6.5 K) and says the base 'assumes heat load for probes'. Each window or arm adds a non-negative load and cold-head capacity is non-decreasing in temperature, so the base temperature is monotone in the number fitted and documented anchors bracket every intermediate configuration: T_base(n) <= T_base(n_hi) for n <= n_hi (sound PASS for any T_req >= T_base(n_hi)), and T_base(n) >= T_base(n_lo) for n >= n_lo (sound FAIL for T_req < T_base(n_lo), but only where T_base(n_lo) is an exact value, not a '<' bound). This replaces a first-principles 300 K Stefan-Boltzmann window load, which is unusable here: sigma T^4 through four 28 mm apertures is 1.13 W against a 0.2 W cold head, yet the OptistatDry reaches 6.5 K, because fused-silica windows (and the CRX's IR-absorbing shield window) block most 300 K radiation and no datasheet gives their IR transmission as a number. The Stefan-Boltzmann value is kept only as a reported upper bound.
proposals.equation_latex: n \le n_{hi} \wedge T_{\mathrm{base}}(n_{hi}) \le T_{\mathrm{req}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{PASS};\quad n \ge n_{lo} \wedge T_{\mathrm{req}} < T_{\mathrm{base}}(n_{lo}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{FAIL};\quad \text{diagnostic: } Q_{\mathrm{win}} \le n_w\,\sigma\,\tfrac{\pi}{4}D^{2}\,T_{\mathrm{amb}}^{4}
proposals.validity: Only for the documented hardware: Spectrosil WF windows on the OptistatDry (other window materials such as ZnSe, CaF2 or KBr transmit more 300 K infrared and are outside the anchors), standard probe-arm anchoring on the CRX-4K. Anchors are typical values. Brackets only - no interpolated temperatures. The blank-fitted values are '<' bounds, so no FAIL can be derived at the low end for the OptistatDry. For the diagnostic, pi enters as a rational upper bound (e.g. 355/113) and sigma = 5.670374419e-8 W m^-2 K^-4 truncated upward.

proposals.title: Laser heating of the probed spot in Raman and PL: dT = B * P <= dT_allowed, with the profile's published no-effect power envelope as a pass gate
proposals.description: For Raman and photoluminescence the relevant laser heat term is the local temperature rise of the probed volume, not the global stage budget (mW lasers against cold heads rated >= 0.16 W). The standard description is a linear laser-heating coefficient B (K/W): Hagiwara et al. measured B ~ 6 C/mW for spinel-hosted and ~1e-2 C/mW for quartz-hosted inclusions and warn that 10 mW can heat absorbing samples by tens to hundreds of degrees; Lax gives a closed form for a Gaussian spot on an absorbing half-space (dT_max = A P / (2 sqrt(pi) kappa w) for surface absorption); Foucher shows thick transparent samples are essentially unaffected while semi-transparent ones can heat more with low-NA objectives. The Raman profile's own source explicitly tested the effect: Pamula et al. ran DI water in the Linkam THMS600 with 532 nm and a 10x/0.25 objective at 5.6, 10 and 28 mW and found the phase-transition temperature unchanged. Model: with a measured B, the fail-capable relation B * P_laser <= dT_allowed; without B, a pass gate P_laser <= 28 mW at the same wavelength and NA (validity only, so powers above the envelope give NEED INFO, never a rejection).
proposals.equation_latex: B\,P_{\mathrm{laser}} \le \Delta T_{\mathrm{allowed}}\quad\text{or (no }B\text{)}\quad \text{gate: } P_{\mathrm{laser}} \le P_{\mathrm{validated}} = 28\,\mathrm{mW},\ \lambda = 532\,\mathrm{nm},\ \mathrm{NA}=0.25;\qquad \text{Lax estimate: } A\,P \le 2\sqrt{\pi}\,\kappa\,w\,\Delta T_{\mathrm{allowed}}
proposals.validity: Steady state; the sample bulk is held at the stage temperature, so the local rise is set by the sample (absorption, conductivity, spot size), not by the cryostat; envelope only for aqueous/transparent samples, 532 nm and NA 0.25 (equality, because Foucher shows lower NA can heat semi-transparent samples more); the Lax form needs a half-space with surface absorption and constant conductivity, and sqrt(pi) must enter as a rational lower bound (e.g. 1.772) in the pass direction and an upper bound (1.7725) in the fail direction.

proposals.title: Eddy-current heating of metallic holders during field sweeps (makes 'temperature stability during field sweep' representable)
proposals.description: A thin metallic disk of radius R, thickness h and resistivity rho in a perpendicular field ramp dB/dt dissipates P = (pi/8) dB/dt^2 h R^4 / rho (Tan, Fermilab note, Eq. 9, valid while the part is thin compared with the skin depth). Written without division: pi * Bdot^2 * h * R^4 <= 8 * rho * P_budget, with the documented maximum charging rate as the worst-case Bdot and P_budget the stage capacity left after other loads. The R^4 scaling is why sub-mK stages are slit: Liu et al. budget Q_eddy = 4.1 nW for a slit 48 mm copper stage at only 1.2e-5 T/s and treat it explicitly in their heat balance. Scaling that example with Bdot^2 shows why the term matters at millikelvin: the same stage at 1 mT/s would dissipate about 28 uW (derived, (1e-3/1.2e-5)^2 x 4.1 nW), more than a Bluefors MXC delivers at 20 mK.
proposals.equation_latex: \pi\,\dot B^{2}\,h\,R^{4} \le 8\,\rho\,P_{\mathrm{budget}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{budget}} = Q(T_{\mathrm{op}}) - L_{\mathrm{other}},\qquad \dot B \le \dot B_{\max}(c)
proposals.validity: Quasi-static: part thin compared with the skin depth / magnetic diffusion time much shorter than the ramp (mu0 sigma h R / 4 << ramp duration); uniform field over the part; resistivity at the operating temperature and field (magnetoresistance increases rho, which is conservative for the load); pi as rational upper bound (355/113) in the pass direction and lower bound in the fail direction (TH3 encoding).

proposals.implementation: Add unit Ohm_m (resistivity) to cryolean/units.py; model eddy_current_sweep_heating with params bdot (T/s, adjustable decrease), holder_radius, holder_thickness (m), holder_resistivity (Ohm m), and the TH3 slot pair for the capacity; status representable_only until a configuration documents both inputs. No Lean change.

proposals.risks: Geometry-specific; slits, wire meshes or non-metallic holders change the result by orders of magnitude; resistivity at mK depends on RRR and field; the formula ignores the field reduction by the eddy currents themselves (conservative for the load).

rejected_ideas: Naive 300 K Stefan-Boltzmann window load as a fail-capable constraint against the documented cooling power: with the documented apertures it gives 1.13 W for the OptistatDry BLV against a 0.2 W cold head and 0.90 W for the CRX against 1 W, yet both reach their documented base temperatures; fused-silica and IR-absorbing windows block most 300 K radiation and no datasheet gives their IR transmission, so the term would produce false rejections (kept only as a diagnostic in TH4/TH6).

A separate radiation or support-post heat term for dilution-refrigerator experiments: Krinner et al. state that both are already included in the specified DR cooling power, so adding them double-counts.

Mount-level dT = P_abs * R_th using thermal.contact_resistance: no configuration documents R_th, so it could only add NEED INFO; for vitrified grids Huebinger shows the heating is set by support-film absorption, not by the stage mount.

Extrapolating Last's thresholds across mesh sizes with the paper's qualitative 1-D model (dT ~ L^2): its own Table 1 scales closer to 1/L (P_max x L = 3870, 3712, 3552 W um/cm2 for 90/58/37 um squares).

Linear 'headroom' extrapolation of the 77 K devitrification threshold to warmer stages, e.g. (136 - 77)/(136 - 78.15) for the THMS600: Mojiri's data imply a steeper drop (~2x from 77 to 95 K, including a mesh change), and the extrapolation would be an inferred estimate that cannot support a pass.

Electron-phonon (hot-electron) heating model for millikelvin transport: device-specific Sigma x volume, dominated by Wiedemann-Franz cooling through the leads, not a cryostat capability; it would create false rejections.
Thermal-lag model for temperature sweeps (POM at 30 K/min, VSM at 5 K/min, Raman up to 100 C/min): needs a sample/stage time constant that no datasheet documents; NEED INFO only.

Latent heat released by freezing samples (Raman/POM) against the LN2 stage capacity: Linkam documents no capacity in W, the latent heat of microlitre samples is negligible, and the procedures do not budget it.
Heat budget of the cryostat microtome (door openings, operator, defrost): Leica gives no W figures; the cryosection profile is decided by the chamber and specimen-head ranges.
VSM eddy heating from the vibrating sample: the field is homogeneous over the vibration amplitude and the published procedure uses a polyethylene capsule; not budgeted.
Thermometer/RuO2 self-heating budget (evidence hl_043-hl_047 already in the repo): thermometer-specific, not a cryostat capability, and it does not change any requirement of the profiles.
TWPA pump-line active load at the MXC inside TH1: the published text gives only '0.1 %, corresponding to 0.02 uW' at the CP; using an upper bound would make failures unsound, so it is omitted.

Window-load and laser dT figures returned by a Tavily research synthesis (e.g. '0.08 W per window', 'dT ~ 0.12 K at 5 mW' for attoDRY, Montana and Optistat CF models): the cited pages, re-read with tavily_extract, do not contain these numbers, so they were discarded as unverified.

Cooling-power curves at more temperatures, missing datasheet values, interval/tolerance representation, QuickXplain/minimal correction sets and SiLA/OPC UA: already covered by the parallel workflow and deliberately not duplicated here.
